text: Ciprofloxacin acts as an off-target inhibitor of the ABL1 tyrosine kinase, the constitutive activation of which—via the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein—drives the uncontrolled myeloid cell proliferation characteristic of Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML). Molecular docking studies indicate that ciprofloxacin binds to the ATP-binding pocket of the ABL1 kinase domain, competing with ATP and stabilizing the inactive conformation of the enzyme. While its binding affinity ($K_d$ in the micromolar range) is significantly lower than that of dedicated tyrosine kinase inhibitors like imatinib, ciprofloxacin exhibits synergistic anti-leukemic effects by inducing apoptosis and inhibiting BCR-ABL1-mediated signaling pathways. Consequently, while not a primary treatment, ciprofloxacin is clinically relevant as it can potentially interfere with CML progression or contribute to drug resistance profiles in patients undergoing concurrent antibiotic therapy.
